data.chapter: Solar System and Space Study Pack
data.sourceTitle: Gravity Holds the Solar System Together
data.targetTitle: Gravity Holds the Solar System Together
data.sourcePassage: The solar system is a connected system made of the Sun and the objects held by the Suns gravity. The Sun contains most of the mass in the solar system, so its gravity strongly affects planets, dwarf planets, moons, asteroids, and comets. Planets do not fall straight into the Sun because they are also moving forward. Gravity pulls them inward while forward motion carries them along, creating curved paths called orbits. The same idea helps explain why moons orbit planets and why human-made satellites can stay in orbit around Earth.

questions.question: What force holds the solar system together?
questions.modelAnswer: Gravity holds the solar system together.

questions.question: Which object contains most of the mass in the solar system?
questions.modelAnswer: The Sun contains most of the mass in the solar system.

questions.question: Why do planets follow curved orbits instead of falling straight into the Sun?
questions.modelAnswer: Planets have forward motion while the Suns gravity pulls them inward, so their paths curve around the Sun.

questions.question: How is a moon orbiting a planet similar to a planet orbiting the Sun?
questions.modelAnswer: Both are examples of one object moving around another because gravity and motion interact.

questions.question: Why is the word system useful for describing the solar system?
questions.modelAnswer: It shows that the Sun, planets, moons, and smaller objects are connected and interact, especially through gravity.

data.chapter: Solar System and Space Study Pack
data.sourcePassage: The eight planets show clear patterns. Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars are the inner planets. They are closer to the Sun, rocky, smaller, and usually have few or no moons. Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune are the outer planets. They are much larger, farther from the Sun, and have many moons. Jupiter and Saturn are gas giants, while Uranus and Neptune are ice giants. Planet data also shows that planets farther from the Sun generally have longer years because they travel around much larger orbits.

questions.question: Name the four inner planets.
questions.modelAnswer: The four inner planets are Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars.

questions.question: Which planet is an ice giant?
questions.modelAnswer: Uranus is an ice giant.

questions.question: Give two differences between inner and outer planets.
questions.modelAnswer: Inner planets are closer to the Sun and rocky, while outer planets are farther away, larger, and have many moons.

questions.question: Why does Neptune have a much longer year than Earth?
questions.modelAnswer: Neptune is much farther from the Sun, so it travels around a much larger orbit and takes longer to complete one revolution.

questions.question: How could planet data support a claim about distance from the Sun and length of year?
questions.modelAnswer: Data can show examples such as Mercury having an 88-day year close to the Sun and Neptune having a 165-year year far from the Sun.

data.chapter: Solar System and Space Study Pack
data.sourcePassage: The Moon does not make its own light. It reflects sunlight. As the Moon orbits Earth, people on Earth see different amounts of the Moons sunlit half. This causes the repeating Moon phase cycle, which takes about 29.5 days from one new moon to the next. Waxing means the visible lit part is growing, and waning means it is shrinking. Moon phases are not caused by Earths shadow. Earths shadow causes a lunar eclipse, which only happens when the Sun, Earth, and Moon line up closely enough.

questions.question: Does the Moon make its own light?
questions.modelAnswer: No. The Moon reflects sunlight.

questions.question: What does waxing mean?
questions.modelAnswer: Waxing means the visible lit part is growing.
options: The Moon is in Earths shadow

questions.question: What causes the normal monthly Moon phase cycle?
questions.modelAnswer: The Moon orbits Earth, so we see different amounts of its sunlit half.

questions.question: Why does a lunar eclipse not happen every month?
questions.modelAnswer: The Sun, Earth, and Moon do not line up exactly most months because the Moons orbit is tilted.

questions.question: How would you correct the idea that Moon phases are caused by Earths shadow?
questions.modelAnswer: Moon phases are caused by the Moon orbiting Earth and changing how much of its sunlit half we see; Earths shadow only causes lunar eclipses.

data.chapter: Solar System and Space Study Pack
data.sourcePassage: Earths seasons are caused mainly by the tilt of Earths axis as Earth revolves around the Sun. When the Northern Hemisphere is tilted toward the Sun, it receives more direct sunlight and has longer days, so it is usually warmer. At the same time, the Southern Hemisphere is tilted away from the Sun and has the opposite season. Tides are a different pattern. They are the regular rise and fall of ocean water caused mostly by the Moons gravity. The Sun also affects tides, but the nearby Moon has the stronger effect.

questions.question: What mainly causes Earths seasons?
questions.modelAnswer: Earths seasons are caused mainly by the tilt of Earths axis as Earth revolves around the Sun.

questions.question: What causes most ocean tides on Earth?
questions.modelAnswer: Most ocean tides are caused by the Moons gravity.

questions.question: Why can the Northern and Southern Hemispheres have opposite seasons?
questions.modelAnswer: When one hemisphere is tilted toward the Sun, the other is tilted away, so they receive different sunlight patterns.

questions.question: Why is distance from the Sun not the main cause of seasons?
questions.modelAnswer: If distance caused seasons, both hemispheres would have the same season at the same time, but they often have opposite seasons.

questions.question: Compare the roles of the Sun and Moon in tides.
questions.modelAnswer: Both affect tides by gravity, but the Moon has the stronger effect because it is much closer to Earth.

data.chapter: Solar System and Space Study Pack
data.sourcePassage: Scientists study space using evidence from tools such as telescopes, satellites, robotic spacecraft, rovers, probes, spectroscopes, and computer models. They cannot visit most objects in space directly, so they use observations, images, measurements, samples, and simulations. Mars is a useful example. Rovers have found rocks and minerals that form in the presence of water, and images show dry river channels and layered rocks. Scientists use this evidence to ask whether Mars once had conditions that could support life. Satellites also help people on Earth by collecting weather, communication, navigation, and Earth observation data.

questions.question: Name one tool scientists use to study space.
questions.modelAnswer: Scientists use tools such as telescopes, satellites, rovers, probes, spectroscopes, and computer models.

questions.question: Which observation could be evidence that Mars once had liquid water?
questions.modelAnswer: Dry river channels can be evidence that Mars once had liquid water.

questions.question: Why are models important in space science?
questions.modelAnswer: Models help scientists explain and predict systems that are too large, far away, slow, or dangerous to study directly.

questions.question: How do satellites help people in everyday life?
questions.modelAnswer: Satellites support GPS, weather forecasts, communication, hurricane tracking, Earth observation, and scientific research.

questions.question: Write a claim and evidence statement about ancient water on Mars.
questions.modelAnswer: Claim: Mars may once have had liquid water. Evidence: rovers found minerals that form with water and images show dry river channels.
